strings.name: Larry Bird
strings.role: Basketball forward · Former coach and team executive
strings.summary: Bird's shooting, passing, rebounding judgment and competitive poise made him Boston's core player, earning three NBA titles and three consecutive regular-season MVPs. His rivalry with Magic Johnson helped expand the NBA's international audience. He later coached and managed Indiana, winning Coach and Executive of the Year awards, and continued as a consultant.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: An NBA champion and Most Valuable Player, and a key star during professional basketball's global expansion.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: West Baden Springs, Indiana, United States.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Three titles and three MVPs
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped Boston win in 1981, 1984 and 1986, with consecutive MVPs from 1984 to 1986.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Played college basketball at Indiana State from 1976 to 1979.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Influence beyond playing
strings.highlights.h2.text: Later won Coach and Executive of the Year awards for contributions to team development.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Bird museum opens
strings.timeline.t1.text: Attended the museum opening in Terre Haute, Indiana.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Returned as Pacers consultant
strings.timeline.t2.text: Resumed basketball advisory work; 2026 reporting still identified him as a consultant.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Executive of the Year
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won the NBA award for his Pacers management work.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Pacers' first NBA Finals
strings.timeline.t4.text: Coached Indiana to the Finals, losing to the Lakers.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Coach of the Year
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the award in his first Pacers coaching season.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Dream Team and retirement
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won Barcelona Olympic gold with the USA and ended his playing career that year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Third title and third straight MVP
strings.timeline.t7.text: Helped Boston win again while completing three consecutive regular-season MVPs.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First NBA title
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the championship alongside Celtics teammates.
strings.timeline.t9.title: College final and NBA beginning
strings.timeline.t9.text: Led Indiana State to the NCAA final before starting his Celtics career.
